import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Check if any feature shows significant association with outcome
    # using Welch's t-test for each feature
    p_values = []
    effects = []
    
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        x = feats.x[:, i]
        y = feats.y
        # Split by outcome
        x0 = x[y == 0]
        x1 = x[y == 1]
        # Welch's t-test
        t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(x1, x0, equal_var=False)
        p_values.append(p_val)
        effects.append(np.mean(x1) - np.mean(x0))
    
    # If no feature is significantly associated, return empty design
    if all(p > 0.05 for p in p_values):
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Find features with p < 0.05 and effect size > 0.1 or < -0.1
    significant_features = []
    for i, (fid, p, effect) in enumerate(zip(feats.ids, p_values, effects)):
        if p < 0.05 and abs(effect) > 0.1:
            significant_features.append((fid, effect, p))
    
    # Sort by effect size (absolute value) descending
    significant_features.sort(key=lambda x: abs(x[1]), reverse=True)
    
    # If no significant features found, return empty design
    if not significant_features:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Check for near-duplicates (correlation >= 0.6)
    # Build correlation matrix
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    # Create set of feature IDs to remove duplicates
    feature_set = set()
    unique_features = []
    for fid, effect, p in significant_features:
        # Check if this feature or its correlated pair is already included
        add_feature = True
        for existing_fid in feature_set:
            idx1 = feats.column(fid)
            idx2 = feats.column(existing_fid)
            if abs(corr_matrix[idx1, idx2]) >= 0.6:
                add_feature = False
                break
        if add_feature:
            feature_set.add(fid)
            unique_features.append((fid, effect, p))
    
    # Take top features up to MAX_DRIVERS
    drivers = tuple(f[0] for f in unique_features[:MAX_DRIVERS])
    
    # For regression columns, include all unique features that are not drivers
    columns = tuple(f[0] for f in unique_features)
    
    # No interaction terms (products) needed for this simple approach
    products = ()
    
    # Simple weighted score based on standardized coefficients
    # Use effect sizes as weights
    loadings = {}
    for fid, effect, p in unique_features:
        loadings[fid] = effect
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
